messages.subject: DIC: Besag, Bym and BYM2
parts:
I have CAR model (spatial only) with both structured and unstructured effects . I have ran this on my data( proportions which are normally distributed- used gaussian distribution)  and compared their DIC values. The besag model+iid and the bym models have positive DIC around +2500. However for the Bym2 the DIC values are about -2000. I would have expected this to be in the same neighborhood as the the besag/bym models. Why the difference and change of direction? 

PS 
Is proper CAR and leroux CAR available in INLA?

Thanks 
Peter

On Mon, 2019-02-04 at 01:55 -0800, Peter Macharia wrote:
> I have CAR model (spatial only) with both structured and unstructured
> effects . I have ran this on my data( proportions which are normally
> distributed- used gaussian distribution) and compared their DIC
> values. The besag model+iid and the bym models have positive DIC
> around +2500. However for the Bym2 the DIC values are about -2000. I
> would have expected this to be in the same neighborhood as the the
> besag/bym models. Why the difference and change of direction?

that is weird. I have never seen this. it could be 'strange' data, as
the bym2 model has very different priors, and you may want to change
these in order to apply it on Gaussian data. This could be the
explanation.
> Is proper CAR and leroux CAR available in INLA?

the proper one, yes, check out inla.doc("besagproper")

I would strongly advise against the Leroux model, as "it does not make
sense" and the 'bym2' is what it should look like.

I try to explain why here: around 36th minute,

http://www.birs.ca/events/2017/5-day-workshops/17w5153/videos/watch/201712040907-Rue.html
